rulings.challenge_claim: This row's span is the whole of chapter 31 (all nine verses), and its medium confidence sits one band above the ceiling the campaign holds for any whole-chapter span.
rulings.grounds: Verified independently from both witnesses' keyed verse maps: chapter 31 carries exactly 9 verses in WEB and exactly 9 in MT, and the row's span runs Isa.31.1-Isa.31.9 -- the complete chapter, with no offset in play (chapter 31 is identity numbering). The row records medium. The campaign caps whole-chapter spans at medium_low, so this is a one-band overshoot, and this row is a named member of the cross-batch whole-chapter class. The challenge is correctly scoped to calibration alone, and that scoping verifies: the seam warrant is genuinely sound and I could not dislodge it. ה֣וֹי is verse-initial at oshb:Isa.31.1 (byte tier) and is the fifth of exactly 6 verse-initial woe onsets across chapters 28-33; the divine frame כִּ֣י כֹ֣ה אָֽמַר יְהוָ֣ה at oshb:Isa.31.4 (byte tier) names the deity as speaker inside its own clause, so it is a divine frame and not one of this book's four royal-messenger uses of the formula; the postpositive שָׂרָ֑יו נְאֻם at oshb:Isa.31.9 (byte tier) is mid-verse and correctly characterised as a signature rather than an onset. Apparatus disclosure verifies as complete for the span -- the marks at oshb:Isa.31.3 and oshb:Isa.31.9, the front-seam mark at oshb:Isa.30.33, all SAMEKH and all correctly typed and unconflated against the single-witness inventory, the paseq at oshb:Isa.31.4 tallied as presence and not placement, and no variant note falls anywhere in chapter 31. So the defect is the band and only the band. Medium severity is right: one band, on a row whose evidence is otherwise the strongest in this cluster.
rulings.remedy: Author wave. (1) confidence: medium to medium_low. This is NOT a one-character edit -- dropping into the low band triggers the campaign's low-band machinery, so the same pass must add the medium_low mirroring across all three sidecars with full schemas (why_low_confidence, concern_type, possible_downstream_risk, suggested_reviewer, proposed_atlas_action, promotion authorities, review states) and a frontier-queue row for this chunk. Write the why_low_confidence text bespoke to the whole-chapter extent, not boilerplate. (2) Bundle into the same pass the two sub-threshold disclosure debts the other lens raised without charging them, since they touch the same fields: splice the imperative address at oshb:Isa.31.6 pointed, שׁ֗וּבוּ לַאֲשֶׁ֛ר הֶעְמִ֥יקוּ סָרָ֖ה בְּנֵ֥י (byte tier), rather than naming it from the English; and disclose the front-seam hook where הֶעְמִ֣יק at oshb:Isa.30.33 and הֶעְמִ֥יקוּ at oshb:Isa.31.6 share an unpointed letter string attested at exactly 2 verses book-wide, with the tier and digit named. Add oshb:Isa.31.6 to boundary_evidence_refs. ORCHESTRATOR NOTE: that hook is a SEAM PAIR at the Isa.30.33|Isa.31.1 edge -- it is the same crossing I upheld from the other side on P08-012 in the preceding attempt. ONE edit across the two rows, matching tier label and matching digit; do not let the two halves be cured separately with divergent wording. No boundary change is proposed on either row. Cure test: a whole-chapter check over the row's span must find the confidence at or below medium_low, and every low-band sidecar and frontier-queue obligation satisfied for this chunk -- the band edit alone does not pass.

rulings.challenge_claim: The onset rests entirely on the English rendering of a particle the row never quotes, the same verse-initial particle is treated as non-structural elsewhere in this same stretch, and the variant note inside the span is undisclosed.
rulings.grounds: The core finding is right and is upheld; two of the three limbs need their framing corrected, and the severity is confirmed rather than moved. UPHELD, and this is the real defect: the row carries no pointed Hebrew anywhere. Its only oshb: refs are the two mark citations, so nothing in it is spliced. What its front seam actually rests on is a topic description read off the English, the preceding unit's closing signature named but never spliced, and tier-3 marks on both sides -- and it records HIGH confidence on that. Under the evidence policy a boundary grounded only on a marker is defective, and tier-3 parashah is never a driver; so the front seam has no tier-1 signal argued in the bytes at all. That is an engagement-class breach carrying a top-band row. FRAMING CORRECTED, limb 1: the challenge says the onset rests on the English rendering of a particle. It does not -- the row never invokes a particle in any form; the presentative is the challenge's own supply of the Hebrew the row should have engaged. That is a legitimate move, but stated as written it credits the row with a driver it does not claim. The particle is genuinely there: oshb:Isa.32.1 opens הֵ֥ן (byte tier), verse-initial at exactly 18 verses book-wide (re-swept independently), so the cure is cheap and the boundary will very likely survive it. FRAMING CORRECTED, limb 2: the cross-site inconsistency verifies exactly -- the only two verse-initial sites of that particle across chapters 28-35 are oshb:Isa.32.1 and הֵ֚ן אֶרְאֶלָּ֔ם at oshb:Isa.33.7 -- but it is not a defect PRESENT in this row, because this row does not use the particle. It is a property of the pair, and more usefully it is a CONSTRAINT ON THE CURE: the moment an author splices the particle here as a driver, the inconsistency with the neighbouring treatment of oshb:Isa.33.7 as internal texture becomes live and must be resolved in the same pass. FORCE REDUCED, limb 3: the variant note at oshb:Isa.32.7 does sit inside the span, staged as the doubled pair עֲנִיִּים֙ בְּאִמְרֵי (the unpointed member at skeleton grade), and the row does not disclose it. But the standing rule is conditional -- check the apparatus before counting or slicing in a variant-bearing verse -- and this row neither quotes nor counts nor slices oshb:Isa.32.7, so no rule is breached. Unlike the asymmetry class, where a row actively works one note and ignores another it covers, this row works none. It is a disclosure-convention debt, worth curing because the neighbouring row does disclose its own in-span note, but it carries no severity. Severity confirmed at medium on limb 1 alone. Not high: the missing signal exists in the bytes and the rear seam is independently tier-1.
rulings.remedy: Author wave. (1) boundary_rationale: splice the onset particle pointed from source with its ref and tier named, and carry its verse-initial digit, so the front seam has a signal in the bytes rather than a topic read from the English; add oshb:Isa.32.1 to boundary_evidence_refs. (2) IN THE SAME PASS, resolve the consistency constraint: if the particle is promoted to a driver here, the row must say what distinguishes this site from the other verse-initial site of the same particle in this stretch, or the driver must be additional to -- not a replacement for -- a stated non-particle ground. Do not cure this row's Hebrew engagement in isolation. (3) confidence: re-decide after (1) and (2) land. High is not carried by a topic description plus tier-3 marks; it may be carried once a tier-1 signal is spliced. Since confidence and the driver set move together, re-check observed_substrate_signals, unit_type and strongest_rejected_alternative as dependent fields. (4) Low priority: disclose the in-span variant note as presence only, single-witness, no reading adjudicated. No boundary change is proposed -- the span itself is not challenged by either lens. Cure test: with every English rendering struck from the row's prose, the front seam must still stand on a spliced pointed form with a named tier -- the test the original fails.

rulings.challenge_claim: The rear edge is placed exactly where the English witness's sentence punctuation falls, with no Hebrew argued, and a three-site token chain runs straight across that edge undisclosed.
rulings.grounds: Both limbs verify from bytes, and the first is a hard rule breach rather than a soft debt. Limb 1: the row's own prose places its rear edge on the ground that two verses form one sentence in the English rendering, and it repeats that criterion in its rejected alternative -- so the boundary criterion IS the English witness's sentence punctuation. Modern punctuation is tier-4 metadata and is NEVER boundary evidence. The challenge is right to press it and right to concede that the conclusion nevertheless survives, because the Hebrew independently carries a subordinating opener at oshb:Isa.32.15, עַד יֵ֨עָרֶ֥ה (byte tier) -- but a true conclusion reached by a forbidden criterion still has to be re-argued. The onset is likewise byte-true and unquoted: oshb:Isa.32.9 opens נָשִׁים֙ שַֽׁאֲנַנּ֔וֹת קֹ֖מְנָה שְׁמַ֣עְנָה קוֹלִ֑י (byte tier), carrying both the vocative and the second-person feminine plural imperative forms the row names from the English alone, and form-class labels are byte-checkable claims owed their pointed form. Limb 1 continued, and this is the sharp part: the row's own syntactic criterion reads past its own close. ר֖וּחַ מִמָּר֑וֹם וְהָיָ֤ה at oshb:Isa.32.15 is continued by וְשָׁכַ֥ן בַּמִּדְבָּ֖ר מִשְׁפָּ֑ט at oshb:Isa.32.16 (byte tier) in the identical waw-plus-perfect pattern, so if syntactic continuity is what binds a verse to its neighbour, it does not stop where the English full stop falls. The criterion is not merely forbidden, it is self-defeating as applied. Limb 2 verifies exactly on an independent re-sweep: שַֽׁאֲנַנּ֔וֹת at oshb:Isa.32.9 and the identical form at oshb:Isa.32.11 are BYTE-identical to each other, and שַׁאֲנַנּֽוֹת at oshb:Isa.32.18 matches them at consonantal-skeleton tier only -- exactly 3 verses book-wide at that tier, the accents differing at the third. Two of the three are this row's own onset evidence and the third sits beyond its close, so a chain the row itself relies on argues continuity across the very edge it cuts, undisclosed. Credited and verified: the row does disclose its in-span variant note at oshb:Isa.32.15 without adjudicating the reading, and mark disclosure is complete -- the PE at oshb:Isa.32.8 ahead of the onset is correctly typed against the single-witness inventory and no mark falls inside the span at all, so there is nothing further owed there. Severity medium is right. The row is honestly held at medium_low and its conclusion survives, but the stated criterion is tier-4 and the cross-seam chain is absent, so the grounds must be rebuilt even though the edge may not move.
rulings.remedy: Author wave. (1) boundary_rationale AND strongest_rejected_alternative: strike the one-sentence-in-the-English criterion from both fields and re-argue the rear edge from the Hebrew -- the subordinating opener at oshb:Isa.32.15 spliced pointed with its tier -- and say explicitly that the modern sentence break is layout, not the ground. (2) Splice the onset pointed at oshb:Isa.32.9 with its tier named, so the vocative and the second-person feminine plural imperative claims rest on the forms rather than on the rendering. (3) Add the cross-seam disclosure for the three-site chain, naming byte tier between the two in-span sites, consonantal-skeleton tier to the site beyond the close, and the 3-verse book-wide digit. Add oshb:Isa.32.9, oshb:Isa.32.11, oshb:Isa.32.15 and oshb:Isa.32.18 to boundary_evidence_refs. (4) Note for the author: the waw-plus-perfect continuation into oshb:Isa.32.16 raises a live question about where this unit actually ends. That is a BOUNDARY question and therefore a PROPOSAL requiring explicit boss adoption -- it is NOT author work and must not be actioned in this pass. Cure the grounds, leave the span. Cure test -- the test that killed the original: with every appeal to the English rendering and its punctuation removed, both the onset and the rear edge must still stand on spliced pointed forms with named tiers, and no criterion may be stated that, applied consistently, would carry the unit past its own close.

rulings.challenge_claim: The front edge is contested by the bytes on three independent counts: the clause chain runs across it, the register change cited to justify it is not located there, and the alternative it rejects is the one the lexical evidence supports.
rulings.grounds: Every count verifies from bytes, every digit and every count-object survives an independent re-derivation, and the row carries no pointed Hebrew at all. This is the strongest challenge in either of my clusters. Count 1 verifies: oshb:Isa.32.16 opens וְשָׁכַ֥ן (byte tier), a waw-plus-perfect continuing ר֖וּחַ מִמָּר֑וֹם וְהָיָ֤ה at oshb:Isa.32.15 inside the same subordinate clause opened by עַד יֵ֨עָרֶ֥ה; nothing verse-initial marks a fresh start. The English adverb at that verse renders the waw form and not an adverb in the text -- re-swept independently, the Hebrew adverb אָ֥ז (oshb:Isa.35.5, byte tier) stands verse-initial at exactly 6 verses book-wide and oshb:Isa.32.16 is not among them. Count 2 verifies exactly, and it is the decisive one because the row's ONLY stated boundary ground is this register change. The last second-person address forms in the stretch are חִרְדוּ֙ שַֽׁאֲנַנּ֔וֹת and the imperatives following them at oshb:Isa.32.11 (byte tier). A form scan of oshb:Isa.32.12 through oshb:Isa.32.15 returns no second-person form: סֹֽפְדִ֑ים at oshb:Isa.32.12 is a masculine plural participle rendered as an imperative by the English witness alone, oshb:Isa.32.13 carries a first-person singular suffix and a third-person feminine verb, oshb:Isa.32.14 carries none, and oshb:Isa.32.15 carries the first-person plural עָלֵ֛ינוּ. So the address the row says governs through Isa.32.15 in fact stops at Isa.32.11 -- four verses ahead of the cut it is used to justify. The row's sole ground is byte-false in its location. Count 3 verifies: שַׁאֲנַנּֽוֹת at oshb:Isa.32.18 rejoins the token opening oshb:Isa.32.9 and oshb:Isa.32.11 at consonantal-skeleton tier, exactly 3 verses book-wide and byte-identical between the first two; and מִבְטַחִ֔ים at oshb:Isa.32.18 -- attested at exactly 1 verse book-wide, so a genuinely unique form -- answers בֹּֽטח֔וֹת at oshb:Isa.32.9 on the same root, that spelling standing at exactly 3 verses book-wide at consonantal-skeleton tier. The challenge names this a root-level observation across two distinct attested spellings rather than a token match, which is the honest description and exactly the tier discipline the campaign requires. The lexical evidence therefore runs toward the grouping the row rejected. Also verified: the closing formula אַשְׁרֵיכֶ֕ם at oshb:Isa.32.20 is byte-true and unquoted, and the challenge's point about the tier-3 mark at that verse holds -- it corroborates a break there equally well under either grouping, so it cannot arbitrate between them, which is precisely why tier-3 is never a driver. HIGH severity is correct and I decline to move it. The row records medium confidence, argues no Hebrew, rests its entire boundary case on one register claim that the bytes locate four verses away, and the independent lexical evidence positively supports the rival it dismisses. That last element is what separates this from the merely-under-argued rows in this cluster: the evidence does not just fail to support the cut, it points the other way.
rulings.remedy: Author wave, grounds only -- and read the scope limit first. (1) boundary_rationale: strike the claim that the second-person plural address drops after Isa.32.15. A form scan places the last second-person forms at oshb:Isa.32.11, so the sentence is byte-false as written and cannot be repaired by rewording; it must be replaced. If a register ground is still wanted, it must be located where the bytes put it and must then explain why the cut falls where it does and not there. (2) Strike or requalify the temporal reading of the row's opening verse: splice וְשָׁכַ֥ן pointed with its tier, name it as a waw-plus-perfect continuation, and state that the English adverb there renders that form rather than the Hebrew adverb, whose 6 verse-initial sites do not include this verse. (3) strongest_rejected_alternative: the rival is currently dismissed on the ground that is byte-false. Re-cut it to engage the actual counter-evidence -- the clause chain across the edge and the two-site root answer into oshb:Isa.32.18 with its 3-verse and 1-verse digits and its tiers named. (4) Splice the closing formula at oshb:Isa.32.20 pointed with its tier. Add oshb:Isa.32.11, oshb:Isa.32.15, oshb:Isa.32.16, oshb:Isa.32.18 and oshb:Isa.32.20 to boundary_evidence_refs. (5) observed_substrate_signals: the topic-onset key is falsified as stated and the blessing-formula key is unevidenced in Hebrew; both re-open, and with them unit_type and confidence. SCOPE LIMIT, binding: this ruling raises a live question whether Isa.32.16 should open a row at all, given that the clause chain and the lexical answer both run across that edge and that the rejected 32:9-32:20 grouping is what the evidence supports. That is a RESPAN and therefore a PROPOSAL requiring explicit boss adoption. It is recorded here as a proposal and is NOT author work; an author must refuse any embedded boundary change and cure the grounds only. The seam is shared with P09-003, so if the boss adopts a respan it lands on both rows as one decision. Cure test -- the test that killed the original: a person-form scan across Isa.32.9-Isa.32.20 must agree with every person claim the row makes, and no boundary ground may be asserted at a verse the scan does not support.

rulings.challenge_claim: The negative that carries this whole-chapter extent -- that no comparable onset interrupts before the next chapter's summons -- is byte-false immediately after both interior segment marks the row dismisses.
rulings.grounds: Verified from bytes at every site, and the challenge's central find is both specific and severe. The row's extent rests on an explicit negative: that no woe, burden, or comparable addressee-vocative onset interrupts before the summons opening the following chapter. That negative is false at three interior sites. oshb:Isa.33.13 opens שִׁמְע֥וּ רְחוֹקִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשִׂ֑יתִי (byte tier), a verse-initial imperative summons with paired addressees; re-swept independently, that imperative stands verse-initial at exactly 10 verses book-wide and at exactly 1 verse across chapters 28-35 -- this one. It is the same formal class as קִרְב֤וּ גוֹיִם֙ לִשְׁמֹ֔עַ וּלְאֻמִּ֖ים הַקְשִׁ֑יבוּ at oshb:Isa.34.1 (byte tier), the very onset the row credits as the next unit's, whose imperative is verse-initial at exactly 3 verses book-wide. oshb:Isa.33.7 opens הֵ֚ן אֶרְאֶלָּ֔ם (byte tier), one of only two verse-initial sites of that presentative across chapters 28-35, the other being the site a neighbouring row uses as its onset driver. And the petition the row itself names begins יְהוָ֥ה חָנֵּ֖נוּ at oshb:Isa.33.2 (byte tier), a divine-name vocative followed by an imperative. The aggravating fact the challenge does not draw out: the row CONTRADICTS ITSELF. Its own device_notes map an internal section beginning at Isa.33.7 and call Isa.33.2-Isa.33.6 a communal petition, then assert in the same breath that the internal turns carry no fresh-addressee marker comparable to the following chapter's summons. Its own map also places a section break at Isa.33.13-Isa.33.14, so it never located the summons at oshb:Isa.33.13 as a section head at all. The load-bearing warrant for the largest span in this cluster is refuted by the row's own contents. Credited and verified: ה֣וֹי שׁוֹדֵ֗ד is verse-initial at oshb:Isa.33.1 (byte tier) and is the sixth of exactly 6 verse-initial woe onsets across chapters 28-33, so the row's digit is correct; עַתָּ֥ה אָק֖וּם יֹאמַ֣ר יְהוָ֑ה at oshb:Isa.33.10 (byte tier) is correctly read as an embedded signature identifying the speaker rather than a narrative or messenger onset; and apparatus disclosure is complete and correctly typed for the whole chapter -- the three SAMEKH marks at Isa.33.1, Isa.33.6 and Isa.33.12 are the only marks in chapter 33, the paseq at Isa.33.14 is the only paseq in chapters 32-35 and is tallied as presence, and no variant note falls in the chapter. The confidence sits AT the whole-chapter cap, not above it -- this row is the corpus's own proof that the writers knew the rule. HIGH severity upheld, and the calibration reasoning matters. Elsewhere in these clusters a byte-false stated ground on a well-marked short span drew medium, because the boundary stood on its own once the bad reason was struck. Here the falsified ground IS the extent: nothing else in the row holds 24 verses together, and there is no independent warrant to fall back on. When the falsified ground is the sole warrant for a maximal span's extent, severity rises. The challenge is right to concede that none of the sites compels a cut -- that concession is why this is a re-argument and not a respan, and it does not lower the severity.
rulings.remedy: Author wave, grounds only. (1) boundary_rationale: strike the blanket negative. It cannot be repaired by softening because the bytes carry the markers it denies; it must be replaced by a positive argument for holding the chapter as one frame -- for example that the woe onset governs a liturgy complex whose interior summons and petitions address the same scene without opening a new frame -- and that argument must NAME the three interior sites it is overriding, spliced pointed with their tiers and their verse-initial digits, rather than denying they exist. (2) Resolve the self-contradiction: the device_notes internal map must agree with whatever the rewritten rationale claims, and the map must be corrected to register the summons at oshb:Isa.33.13, which it currently misses entirely. (3) Add oshb:Isa.33.2, oshb:Isa.33.7 and oshb:Isa.33.13 to boundary_evidence_refs. (4) Leave the confidence at medium_low -- it is already at the cap and the low-band sidecar and frontier-queue obligations for this chunk should be confirmed present rather than re-created. SCOPE LIMIT: whether oshb:Isa.33.13 opens a unit is a BOUNDARY question and therefore a PROPOSAL requiring explicit boss adoption; it is recorded as such and is NOT author work. The other lens supported this row's bounds and the challenge concedes no cut is compelled, so the presumption is that the span holds and only the argument changes. Cure test -- the test that killed the original: sweep the row's own span for verse-initial imperative-summons, vocative and presentative onsets, and every site the sweep returns must be named and addressed somewhere in the row; no universal negative may stand that the sweep contradicts.

rulings.challenge_claim: LF: this row's span is the whole of chapter 34 (all seventeen verses) and its high confidence sits two bands above the whole-chapter ceiling. OL: the row's own onset class recurs verse-initially inside the span at an undisclosed site, no Hebrew is quoted anywhere, and the whole-chapter extent is carried at the top confidence band.
rulings.grounds: Both are upheld. The two lenses CONVERGE on one defect -- the whole-chapter extent at the top band -- and the other lens adds two distinct findings on top of it. Convergent limb, verified independently from both witnesses' verse maps: chapter 34 carries exactly 17 verses in WEB and exactly 17 in MT, and the span runs Isa.34.1-Isa.34.17, the complete chapter under identity numbering. The row records high against a medium_low ceiling -- a TWO-band overshoot, and this row is a named member of the cross-batch whole-chapter class. Distinct limb A, verified: the row carries no pointed Hebrew anywhere. Its only oshb: ref is a single mark citation; the onset, the addressee shift and the register change at the close are all argued from English renderings. The onset is in fact byte-true -- oshb:Isa.34.1 opens קִרְב֤וּ גוֹיִם֙ לִשְׁמֹ֔עַ וּלְאֻמִּ֖ים הַקְשִׁ֑יבוּ (byte tier), verse-initial imperatives with their vocatives, that imperative standing verse-initial at exactly 3 verses book-wide on an independent re-sweep -- which makes the omission gratuitous rather than difficult. Distinct limb B, verified: the row's negative is written to exclude comparable onsets through the whole chapter, and oshb:Isa.34.16 opens דִּרְשׁ֨וּ מֵֽעַל סֵ֤פֶר יְהוָה֙ וּֽקְרָ֔אוּ (byte tier), a verse-initial imperative pair, that imperative standing verse-initial at exactly 2 verses book-wide with its only other site elsewhere in the book. The other lens is scrupulous here and I confirm the concession: that site carries no vocative, so it is formally weaker than the row's own onset and does not force a cut -- but it is the same imperative-onset class the row uses for itself, and a negative written to exclude that class owes it a disclosure. Credited and verified: apparatus disclosure is complete and correctly typed -- the SAMEKH at oshb:Isa.34.17 is the only mark in chapter 34, no paseq and no variant note falls anywhere in the chapter, and the front seam at Isa.33.24 carries no mark, so nothing further is owed. The other lens also makes a fair point that the row's own rejected alternative, weighing a narrowing turn inside the span, is itself evidence that a real internal question was live -- which tells against the top band independently of the cap. HIGH severity. A two-band cap overshoot is on its own the more serious of the two whole-chapter violations I have seen at one band, and the undisclosed interior onset is exactly the exposure the cap exists to price.
rulings.remedy: Author wave, one pass, no boundary change proposed by either lens. (1) confidence: high to medium_low, a two-band drop. As with the other members of this class the band edit alone does not discharge it -- the same pass must add the low-band mirroring across all three sidecars with full schemas and a frontier-queue row for this chunk, with bespoke why_low_confidence text keyed to the whole-chapter extent and to the interior onset below. (2) Splice the onset pointed at oshb:Isa.34.1 with its tier named and its verse-initial digit, so the row's driver rests on the forms rather than on the rendering; add oshb:Isa.34.1 to boundary_evidence_refs. (3) Rewrite the negative so it names the interior imperative onset at oshb:Isa.34.16 rather than excluding it by silence, spliced pointed with its tier and its 2-verse book-wide digit, and states why the row holds across it -- the absence of a vocative there against the vocative-bearing onset at Isa.34.1. Add oshb:Isa.34.16 to boundary_evidence_refs. Cure test -- the test that killed the original: a verse-initial imperative-onset sweep across the row's own span must return oshb:Isa.34.16, and the row must name and address every site it returns; and a whole-chapter check must find the confidence at or below medium_low with the low-band sidecar and frontier-queue obligations satisfied.

rulings.challenge_claim: LF: this row's span is the whole of chapter 35 (all ten verses) at high confidence, two bands above the whole-chapter ceiling, and its own closing quotation of Isa.35.10 inserts a stray quotation mark not present in the source. OL: the rejected alternative turns on one English adverb doing two different jobs with no counterpart in the Hebrew, and a second imperative onset inside the span goes unnamed.
rulings.grounds: Both are upheld. The lenses CONVERGE on the whole-chapter band and each adds a distinct finding the other misses. Convergent limb, verified from both witnesses' verse maps: chapter 35 carries exactly 10 verses in WEB and exactly 10 in MT, and the span runs Isa.35.1-Isa.35.10, the complete chapter under identity numbering, recorded at high against a medium_low ceiling -- a TWO-band overshoot, this row being a named member of the cross-batch whole-chapter class. Distinct limb A, character-level byte-check performed and CONFIRMED. The source verse at web:Isa.35.10 ends on a period followed by exactly one character, U+201D, the curly right double quotation mark closing a speech opened by the U+201C at web:Isa.35.4 and left open across the intervening verses; the source verse contains no U+0022 anywhere. The row's own quotation of that same clause ends on a period, then U+0022, then U+201D -- one straight double-quote character inserted that is absent from the source, and it is the only U+0022 in the row's entire prose. The breach lands on the row's own boundary-closing citation, which is the citation doing the most work in the field. The other lens is right that it does not disturb the seam determination, and right that the close is independently carried. Distinct limb B, verified exactly on an independent re-sweep.
